# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money and runs have a request limit. Batch independent
   tool calls in one turn, write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in
   one round. When several files need changes, send ALL the edit_file calls in ONE reply (several tool
   calls in the same message), never one edit per reply.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.
10. State changes vs messages: compute every value a user-visible message needs (e.g. the expected value
   of the item that was just submitted, the name of the record just deleted) BEFORE you advance or mutate
   state, and build the message from those saved values. Write a test for every user-visible message that
   asserts it refers to the RIGHT item — including the wrong-input path (e.g. an incorrect submission shows
   that same item's expected value, not the next item's).

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Visual style comes from YOUR UI design brief (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md section 5), derived from this spec's
  users and domain — not from any fixed template. Put the palette and fonts in one module (ui/theme.py) and
  use it everywhere; never leave the default grey Tk look.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- High-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding, flat relief and a hover colour (bind
  <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Where a flow ends (a round, a task, a booking…), show a clear result / summary screen whose message and
  rating match the actual outcome (no praise and no positive rating for a zero or failing result).
- Forms: every text input has a clearly visible Submit/Check button next to it, the main input has keyboard
  focus, Enter also submits, the input is cleared automatically after each submission, and feedback is clear
  and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself. Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Add/edit forms: include an input for EVERY field the entity needs to work (e.g. for a quiz item: prompt,
  correct value, kind, and the choices when it has choices). Never fill a required field silently with a
  hard-coded default; validate the input and show an error in the form instead. Test adding and editing an item
  through the form and then using it.
- Never ship empty: provide sensible seed data (data/*.json or SQL inserts) that is loaded automatically on first
  start when the store is empty, enough to use every feature immediately (for a quiz-style app at least 20
  items covering every kind). Test that a fresh database is seeded.
- Quiz / practice apps (any domain): every round draws its items at RANDOM from the whole pool (seed items AND
  items added by an admin/user) and SHUFFLES their order, so two rounds are not the same. If the content is
  computable (math, arithmetic, number patterns, unit conversions…), the app ALSO generates new items in code
  for every round: the correct value is calculated in code, and wrong choices are distinct and never equal to
  (or equivalent to) the correct value. If the content is not computable, draw randomly from the pool and
  shuffle. Tests: two rounds differ (seeded random), admin-added items can appear in a round, and every
  generated item has a correct computed value and valid distinct choices. Generator tests must RECOMPUTE the
  expected value independently from the item's own data (parse its operands and calculate again) for each kind
  over many random seeds, not just check that the stored answer is among the choices; reject ambiguous items
  (e.g. two equal operands in a "which is larger" item).
- Text inputs must be clearly visible: their background differs from the surrounding container or they have a
  visible border (relief + borderwidth, or highlightthickness with a contrasting highlight colour).
- Window title: `create_app(root)` sets root.title() to the application's real name, never the default "tk".
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Contract (the harness
  uses it): ui/app.py defines `create_app(root) -> App`, which builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop();
  App has `screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `show(name)`. Every screen must render safely when shown
  directly (e.g. a results or detail screen shown before any data exists displays defaults, not a crash).
- Canvas drawing: winfo_width()/winfo_height() return 1 until the window is actually shown, so NEVER compute
  positions from them at construction time. Bind <Configure> on the canvas and (re)draw backgrounds,
  decorations, shapes and canvas text from event.width/event.height; lay out normal widgets with pack/grid or
  place(relx=…, rely=…). The harness opens the real window at 1280x800 AND at the minimum size (1100x750),
  shows every screen and FAILS verification if widgets or canvas items are outside the visible area or squeezed
  into a corner, a button has no room or its text is cut off, a button covers text, a text input has no
  visible submit button, or a Tk callback raises. Design every screen to fit 1100x750 (scroll long content).
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's widgets
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one CORRECT
  and one WRONG form submission (input cleared; feedback text names the expected value of the item just
  submitted), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.
- Geometry managers: NEVER mix pack and grid for widgets that share the same parent container (Tk raises
  "cannot use geometry manager grid inside … managed by pack" and the screen stops updating). When a screen
  switches between layouts (e.g. a text input vs. a grid of choice buttons), give each layout its own inner
  frame, or destroy/forget the previous widgets BEFORE adding the new ones.
- The UI smoke test must also play ONE complete flow from the start screen to the result screen through the
  UI's own callbacks, covering every variant the app has (e.g. typed and choice inputs, in an order that
  switches between them). Pump root.update() for real time so the app's own after() timers run, and record
  errors with root.report_callback_exception; assert that no Tk callback error occurred.
- Text-heavy screens: buttons must never cover text. Put long text in a frame laid out with pack/grid (or a
  scrollable Text) ABOVE the button row instead of placing a button at a fixed position over it.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- The harness also imports every module and loads main.py (without running main()); any ImportError,
  AttributeError or NameError at import time fails verification. Only import names that really exist, and keep
  main.py's start-up code under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
- Change project files only with write_files / edit_file / delete_file. run_python scripts are for checks and
  diagnostics; they must not create, modify or delete project files. Delete temporary helper files with
  delete_file before finish.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files loaded on first start (required whenever the app manages content)
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).
  5. "UI design brief" derived from the spec (actors, use cases, domain, any task profile): target users,
     mood, colour palette (hex values with roles: background, surface, primary, accent, success, error,
     text), fonts and sizes, layout approach, key screens and navigation. Fit the app, e.g.:
     Tic-Tac-Toe → playful, a big 3x3 board, bold contrasting X/O colours; library tracker → clean and calm,
     table/list based, neutral palette with one accent; learning app → bright, encouraging, big friendly
     controls. The implementation must follow this brief.

## PHASE 1/3 — ANALYSE & PLAN (plan mode: read-only)
Reconcile the spec with the desktop constraint and write the UI design brief: who uses this app, what
mood suits it, and which palette, fonts, layout and screens follow from that. Then, in as few turns as
possible:
1. Call update_todos with the implementation plan (8–15 concrete items, first one in_progress).
2. Call submit_plan with:
   - design_decisions: the full Markdown content of DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (see the output contract),
     including section 5 "UI design brief",
   - file_tree: every file you will create (relative paths),
   - notes: short content for AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions, module responsibilities, conventions).
You may call both tools in the same turn.
I'll analyze the spec and create a plan. Let me first check the project directory.

## 3. Assumptions (spec is thin)

- **Space Fractions** is an educational fraction game for a single local user (End User) with an optional Admin role for updating questions.

- Questions are both **seeded** (data/questions.json, ≥20 items covering types: compare, addition, subtraction, multiplication, simplify, identify) and **code-generated** at runtime: math fraction questions where the correct value is computed in code and validated independently in tests. Wrong choices are distinct and never equal to the correct value.
- Question kinds: `compare` (which is larger/smaller), `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `simplify`, `equivalent`. Each generated item stores its operands so tests can RECOMPUTE the expected answer.
- **Admin** updates questions via an admin screen (add/edit/delete), persisted to SQLite; generated questions are not editable (computed) but seed/added questions form the pool.
- "Introductory movie", "main menu", "ending scene with feedback" are realised as Tkinter screens (intro/title with animated stars, menu, results/ending screen with score + encouraging/calibrated feedback).
- 1000 concurrent users / 1-hour sessions (A1, A2) are not applicable to single-user desktop; noted as non-goals. Session time is not enforced.
- Persistence: scores history in `games` table; questions in `questions` table; profile in `users` table (ASR-1 durability).

| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin update → success) | `admin/admin.py` + `ui/screens/admin_screen.py` |

## 5. UI design brief

- **Target users**: children/students aged ~8–12 (End User) learning fractions, plus a teacher/parent (Admin) who updates questions. Single local user.
- **Mood**: bright, playful, encouraging, space-themed (fits "Space Fractions" title) — a fun learning game, not a serious test.
- **Colour palette** (roles):
  - background: `#0B1026` (deep space navy)
  - surface: `#1B2144` (panel background)
  - primary: `#4A90E2` (buttons, accents)
  - accent: `#FFD166` (stars, highlights, score)
  - secondary accent: `#9B5DE5` (space purple)
  - success: `#43D17C` (correct feedback)
  - error: `#FF5D73` (wrong feedback)
  - text: `#F4F6FF` (light, high contrast)
  - muted text: `#A9B4D6`
- **Fonts**: Tk defaults via `tkinter.font`; sizes: title 40 bold, subtitle 26, main content 26, buttons 20, inputs 20, feedback 24. Use `('Segoe UI', size, weight)`.
- **Layout**: fixed full window (minsize 1100x750, centered, maximized). Each screen a `tk.Frame`; navigation via controller `ui/app.py`. Title header bar top, content center, big buttons bottom. Canvas space background with animated stars drawn on `<Configure>`.
- **Key screens**:
  1. IntroScreen (introductory movie: animated starfield + title + "Start").
  2. MenuScreen (main menu: Play, View Score, Help, Admin, Quit).
  3. GameScreen (prompt + typed OR multiple-choice input, big submit button, Enter submits, input auto-clears, immediate green/red feedback).
  4. PauseScreen / HelpScreen (paused state, resume).
  5. ResultsScreen (ending scene: score, calibrated feedback — no praise for 0, stars for high score).
  6. AdminScreen (list/add/edit/delete questions, validate all fields).
  7. ScoreHistoryScreen (past scores from SQLite).
- **Feedback policy**: correct → green "Correct!" with the right value; wrong → red showing the expected value of the *just-submitted* item (computed before state advances). Ending screen rating matches actual score (0 = "Let's practice more", high = celebratory stars).

{"files": [{"content": """"Code-generated fraction questions.

Every generated question carries its operands so tests can RECOMPUTE the expected
answer independently. Wrong choices are distinct and never equal (or equivalent) to
the correct value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List

from question.question import Question, QuestionKind


def _frac(a: int, b: int) -> Fraction:
    return Fraction(a, b)


def _fmt(f: Fraction) -> str:
    if f.denominator == 1:
        return str(f.numerator)
    return f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"


def _make_wrong(correct: Fraction, want: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    """Distinct wrong choices, none equivalent to the correct value."""
    out: list[str] = []
    target = correct
    seen = {Fraction(correct)}
    attempts = 0
    while len(out) < want and attempts < 500:
        attempts += 1
        delta = rng.randint(1, 5)
        num = correct.numerator + rng.choice([-delta, delta])
        den = correct.denominator
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            den += rng.randint(1, 4)
        if den == 0:
            continue
        cand = Fraction(num, den)
        if cand <= 0 or cand in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(cand)
        out.append(_fmt(cand))
    # Fallback if not enough distinct values were produced.
    fallback_den = correct.denominator + 1
    while len(out) < want:
        cand = Fraction(correct.numerator + len(out) + 1, fallback_den)
        if cand <= 0 or cand in seen:
            fallback_den += 1
            continue
        seen.add(cand)
        out.append(_fmt(cand))
    return out


def _gen_compare(rng: random.Random) -> Question:
    # distinct operands so there is always an unambiguous larger/smaller value

        self._default_total = default_total
        self._game: Optional[Game] = None

        n = total or self._default_total
        questions = build_round(self._pool, total=n)
        self._game = Game(id=str(uuid.uuid4()), questions=questions)
        self._state = GameStateMachine()  # starts Playing

    def pause(self) -> None:
        self._state.pause()

    def resume(self) -> None:
        self._state.resume()

    def current_question(self) -> Optional[Question]:
        if self._game is None:
            return None
        return self._game.current_question

    def submit(self, answer: str) -> Optional[AnswerResult]:
        """Submit an answer for the current question; returns result BEFORE advance."""
        if self._game is None:
            return None
        q = self._game.current_question
        if q is None:
            return None
        correct = q.checkAnswer(answer)
        # Build result using the just-submitted item's values BEFORE mutating state.
        result = AnswerResult(
            correct=correct,
            submitted=answer.strip(),
            expected=q.correct,
            prompt=q.prompt,
            score=self._game.viewScore(),
            total=self._game.total,
        )
        self._game.submitAnswer(answer)
        if self._game.is_finished:
            self._state.gameOver()
        if self._game.is_finished:
            result.score = self._game.viewScore()
        return result

        return self._game.viewScore() if self._game else 0

    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "questions.json"

    """CRUD for persisted questions plus seed auto-load on empty store."""

    def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[str] = None):
        if db_path is None:
            db_path = str(_data_dir() / "space_fractions.db")
        self._db_path = db_path
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        self._conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
        self._conn.commit()
        self._seed_if_empty()

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._conn.close()

    def _seed_if_empty(self) -> None:
        cur = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM questions")
        if cur.fetchone()[0] > 0:
            return
        seed = _seed_file()
        if seed.exists():
            data = json.loads(seed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            for item in data.get("questions", []):
                self._insert(Question.from_kwargs(**item))
            self._ensure_default_user()

    def _ensure_default_user(self) -> None:
        self._conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (id, username, role) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            ("u-default", "Player", "user"),
        )
        self._conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (id, username, role) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            ("u-admin", "Admin", "admin"),
        )
        self._conn.commit()

    def _insert(self, q: Question) -> None:
        self._conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO questions (id, prompt, correct, options, kind) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (q.id, q.prompt, q.correct, json.dumps(q.options), q.kind.value),
        )

    def list_all(self) -> List[Question]:
        rows = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, prompt, correct, options, kind FROM questions ORDER BY id"
        ).fetchall()
        out = []
        for rid, prompt, correct, options, kind in rows:
            out.append(
                Question(
                    id=rid,
                    prompt=prompt,
                    correct=correct,
                    options=json.loads(options),
                    kind=QuestionKind(kind),
                )
            )
        return out

    def add(self, q: Question) -> List[str]:
        errors = q.validate()
        if errors:
            return errors
        self._insert(q)
        self._conn.commit()
        return []

    def update(self, q: Question) -> List[str]:
        errors = q.validate()
        if errors:
            return errors
        self._insert(q)
        self._conn.commit()
        return []

    def delete(self, question_id: str) -> bool:
        cur = self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (question_id,))
        self._conn.commit()
        return cur.rowcount > 0

            "INSERT INTO games (id, username, score, total, played_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",

                score,
                total,
                datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),

        ).fetchall()
        return [

            for u, s, t, p in rows
        ]

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import tkinter as tk

from ui import theme


class StarCanvas(tk.Canvas):
    """Animated space starfield; draws on <Configure> so it is resizable-safe."""

    def __init__(self, master, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("bg", theme.BACKGROUND)
        kwargs.setdefault("highlightthickness", 0)
        super().__init__(master, **kwargs)
        self._rng = random.Random(1234)
        self._stars: list[tuple[float, float, float, int]] = []
        self._after_id = None
        self.bind("<Configure>", self._on_configure)

    def _on_configure(self, event):
        w, h = event.width, event.height
        if w <= 1 or h <= 1:
            return
        self.delete("all")
        self._stars = [
            (self._rng.random(), self._rng.random(), self._rng.random(), w + h)
            for _ in range(140)
        ]
        self._draw(w, h)

    def _draw(self, w: int, h: int):
        if w <= 1 or h <= 1:
            return
        self.delete("all")
        phase = getattr(self, "_phase", 0.0)
        for sx, sy, size, _ in self._stars:
            x = sx * w
            y = (sy * h + phase * 240) % h
            r = 1 + size % 2
            self.create_oval(x - r, y - r, x + r, y + r, fill=theme.TEXT, outline="")
        self._phase = phase + 0.02
        self._after_id = self.after(50, lambda: self._draw(w, h))

    def destroy(self):
        if self._after_id is not None:
            try:
                self.after_cancel(self._after_id)
            except Exception:
                pass
        super().destroy()

from __future__ import annotations

import tkinter as tk

from question.question import Question, QuestionKind
from ui import theme


class AdminScreen(tk.Frame):
    def __init__(self, master, app):
        super().__init__(master, bg=theme.BACKGROUND)
        self.app = app
        self.editing_id = None

        self.title = tk.Label(self, text="Admin: Update Questions",
                              bg=theme.BACKGROUND, fg=theme.ACCENT,
                              font=theme.SUBTITLE_FONT)
        self.title.pack(pady=(20, 10))

        # Form (every field the entity needs)
        form = tk.Frame(self, bg=theme.BACKGROUND)
        form.pack(pady=10)
        self._make_label_entry(form, "Prompt", 0, self.prompt_var := tk.StringVar())
        self._make_label_entry(form, "Correct value", 1, self.correct_var := tk.StringVar())
        self._make_label_entry(form, "Options (comma separated)", 2, self.options_var := tk.StringVar())
        self._make_label_entry(form, "Kind", 3, self.kind_var := tk.StringVar(value="compare"))

        self.feedback = tk.Label(self, text="", bg=theme.BACKGROUND,
                                 fg=theme.ERROR, font=theme.FEEDBACK_FONT)
        self.feedback.pack(pady=5)

        btnrow = tk.Frame(self, bg=theme.BACKGROUND)
        btnrow.pack(pady=10)
        self.add_btn = tk.Button(btnrow, text="Add Question", command=self._add)
        theme.style_button(self.add_btn)
        self.add_btn.pack(side="left", padx=6)
        self.save_btn = tk.Button(btnrow, text="Save Edit", command=self._save)
        theme.style_button(self.save_btn)
        self.save_btn.pack(side="left", padx=6)

        # List of questions
        self.listbox = tk.Listbox(self, bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
                                  font=theme.SMALL_FONT, height=10,
                                  selectbackground=theme.PRIMARY)
        self.listbox.pack(pady=10, fill="both", expand=True, padx=30)

        editrow = tk.Frame(self, bg=theme.BACKGROUND)
        editrow.pack(pady=6)
        self.edit_btn = tk.Button(editrow, text="Load Selected", command=self._load)
        theme.style_button(self.edit_btn)
        self.edit_btn.pack(side="left", padx=6)
        self.delete_btn = tk.Button(editrow, text="Delete Selected", command=self._delete)
        theme.style_button(self.delete_btn)
        self.delete_btn.configure(bg=theme.ERROR, activebackground=theme.ERROR)
        self.delete_btn.pack(side="left", padx=6)

        self.back_btn = tk.Button(self, text="Back to Menu",
                                  command=lambda: self.app.show("menu"))
        theme.style_button(self.back_btn)
        self.back_btn.pack(pady=12)

    def _make_label_entry(self, parent, label, row, var):
        tk.Label(parent, text=label, bg=theme.BACKGROUND, fg=theme.MUTED,
                 font=theme.LABEL_FONT).grid(row=row, column=0, sticky="e", padx=6, pady=4)
        e = tk.Entry(parent, textvariable=var, width=40)
        theme.style_entry(e)
        e.grid(row=row, column=1, padx=6, pady=4)

    def begin(self):
        self._refresh()

    def _refresh(self):
        self.listbox.delete(0, "end")
        for q in self.app.repo.list_all():
            self.listbox.insert("end", f"{q.id} | {q.prompt}")

    def _selected_id(self):
        sel = self.listbox.curselection()
        if not sel:
            return None
        text = self.listbox.get(sel[0])
        return text.split(" | ", 1)[0]

    def _clear_form(self):
        self.editing_id = None
        for var in (self.prompt_var, self.correct_var, self.options_var):
            var.set("")
        self.kind_var.set("compare")
        self.feedback.configure(text="")

    def _make_question(self) -> Question:
        options = [o.strip() for o in self.options_var.get().split(",") if o.strip()]
        kind = self.kind_var.get().strip().lower() or "compare"
        try:
            kind_enum = QuestionKind(kind)
        except ValueError:
            kind_enum = QuestionKind.COMPARE
        q = Question(
            id=self.editing_id or f"q-{len(self.app.repo.list_all()) + 1}",
            prompt=self.prompt_var.get().strip(),
            correct=self.correct_var.get().strip(),
            options=options,
            kind=kind_enum,
        )
        return q

    def _add(self):
        q = self._make_question()
        errors = self.app.repo.add(q)
        if errors:
            self.feedback.configure(text="; ".join(errors), fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        self.feedback.configure(text=f"Added: {q.prompt}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        self._clear_form()
        self._refresh()

    def _load(self):
        qid = self._selected_id()
        if not qid:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Select a question first", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        for q in self.app.repo.list_all():
            if q.id == qid:
                self.editing_id = q.id
                self.prompt_var.set(q.prompt)
                self.correct_var.set(q.correct)
                self.options_var.set(", ".join(q.options))
                self.kind_var.set(q.kind.value)
                self.feedback.configure(text=f"Editing {q.id}", fg=theme.MUTED)
                return

    def _save(self):
        if not self.editing_id:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Load a question to edit first", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        q = self._make_question()
        errors = self.app.repo.update(q)
        if errors:
            self.feedback.configure(text="; ".join(errors), fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        self.feedback.configure(text=f"Saved: {q.prompt}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        self._clear_form()
        self._refresh()

    def _delete(self):
        qid = self._selected_id()
        if not qid:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Select a question first", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        removed = self.app.repo.delete(qid)
        if removed:
            self.feedback.configure(text=f"Deleted {qid}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        else:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Could not delete", fg=theme.ERROR)
        self._clear_form()
        self._refresh()

from __future__ import annotations

import tkinter as tk
from typing import Dict

from game.service import GameService
from question.repository import QuestionRepository
from ui import theme


class App:
    def __init__(self, root: tk.Tk):
        self.root = root
        root.title("Space Fractions")
        root.minsize(1100, 750)
        self.repo = QuestionRepository()
        self.service = GameService(pool=self.repo.list_all(), default_total=5)

        container = tk.Frame(root, bg=theme.BACKGROUND)
        container.pack(fill="both", expand=True)

        self.screens: Dict[str, tk.Frame] = {}
        self._build_screens(container)
        self.show("intro")

    def _build_screens(self, container):
        from ui.screens.intro_screen import IntroScreen
        from ui.screens.menu_screen import MenuScreen
        from ui.screens.game_screen import GameScreen
        from ui.screens.pause_screen import PauseScreen
        from ui.screens.results_screen import ResultsScreen
        from ui.screens.help_screen import HelpScreen
        from ui.screens.score_screen import ScoreScreen
        from ui.screens.admin_screen import AdminScreen

        self.screens["intro"] = IntroScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["menu"] = MenuScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["game"] = GameScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["pause"] = PauseScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["results"] = ResultsScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["help"] = HelpScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["score"] = ScoreScreen(container, self)
        self.screens["admin"] = AdminScreen(container, self)

    def show(self, name: str):
        for key, frame in self.screens.items():
            if key == name:
                frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
            else:
                frame.pack_forget()
        screen = self.screens[name]
        screen.tkraise()
        begin = getattr(screen, "begin", None)
        if callable(begin):
            begin()

    def quit(self):
        self.repo.close()
        self.root.destroy()


def create_app(root: tk.Tk) -> App:
    """Build the application without calling mainloop()."""
    app = App(root)
    # F11 fullscreen, Esc exits fullscreen
    def toggle_fullscreen(_event=None):
        cur = root.attributes("-fullscreen")
        root.attributes("-fullscreen", not cur)

    def exit_fullscreen(_event=None):
        root.attributes("-fullscreen", False)

    root.bind("<F11>", toggle_fullscreen)
    root.bind("<Escape>", exit_fullscreen)
    return app

import random

def _parse(s):
    return Fraction(s)


def test_generated_compare_valid():
    for seed in range(200):
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        q = generator.generate_question(rng)
        if q.kind is not QuestionKind.COMPARE:
            continue
        a = _parse(q.operands["a"])
        b = _parse(q.operands["b"])
        which = q.operands["which"]
        expected = max(a, b) if which == "larger" else min(a, b)
        # assert operands are distinct for an unambiguous item
        assert a != b, f"ambiguous compare at seed {seed}"
        assert _parse(q.correct) == expected
        assert q.correct in q.options
        # all options distinct and none equivalent to correct
        opts = [_parse(o) for o in q.options]
        assert len(set(opts)) == len(opts)
        assert all(o != expected for o in opts if o != expected)


def test_generated_arithmetic_valid():
    for seed in range(200):
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        q = generator.generate_question(rng)
        if q.kind not in (QuestionKind.ADD, QuestionKind.SUBTRACT, QuestionKind.MULTIPLY):
            continue
        a = _parse(q.operands["a"])
        b = _parse(q.operands["b"])
        op = q.operands["op"]
        if op == "+":
            expected = a + b
        elif op == "-":
            expected = a - b
            assert expected >= 0
        else:
            expected = a * b
        assert _parse(q.correct) == expected
        opts = [_parse(o) for o in q.options]
        assert len(set(opts)) == len(opts)
        assert sum(1 for o in opts if o == expected) == 1

    for seed in range(200):

        if q.kind is not QuestionKind.SIMPLIFY:

        num = q.operands["num"]
        den = q.operands["den"]
        expected = Fraction(num, den)
        assert _parse(q.correct) == expected
        opts = [_parse(o) for o in q.options]
        assert len(set(opts)) == len(opts)

    for seed in range(200):
        rng = random.Random(seed)

# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md

## 1. Adaptation table (web/cloud → desktop)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| web-based (REST/gRPC service) | single-process desktop app, in-process function calls | task constraint: Windows desktop deliverable |
| microservices (Game/Question/User/Admin) | Python packages `game`, `question`, `user`, `admin` | logical components kept as modules |
| Node.js 18-20 runtime | Python 3.11+, stdlib only | bundled exe constraint |
| Express.js 4-5 web framework | Tkinter `ui/` screens | desktop GUI |
| RESTful API (`openapi.yaml`, `/play`) | in-process `GameService` with same operations (Play, ViewScore) | interface preserved, transport removed |
| gRPC `internal.proto` (GameService.Play) | `game/service.py` `GameService.play(request)` | same operation, no network |
| PostgreSQL 14-15 (`games`, `question` tables) | SQLite file via `sqlite3` (`sql/schema.sql`) | stdlib persistence |
| Redis cache | in-memory `random`/lists | single-user, no shared cache needed |
| RabbitMQ messaging | direct method calls | no async workers needed |
| Elasticsearch search | `sqlite3` queries + in-memory filters | question admin search |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | single local user profile (username), Admin vs User role | single local user per session |
| Prometheus observability | `logging` to stdout/file | stdlib |
| Jenkins CI/CD | `run_python test` + pytest | harness handles CI |
| Docker 20-21 | optional `Dockerfile` (python:3.12-slim) running tests | headless test image |
| Terraform / Kubernetes / replicas / Istio / Vault / TLS | n/a (single-user desktop) | no distributed deployment |
| `sql/question_ddl.sql` (referenced but not delivered) | `sql/schema.sql` with `questions` + `games` + `users` tables | persistence for question data & scores (ASR-1) |

## 2. Input issues found

| Code | Handling |
|---|---|
| EMPTY_TABLE (unit/integration/… chaos matrix empty) | Filled a concrete testing matrix in README/TRACEABILITY mapping each test type to Game/Question components and files. |
| ARTIFACT_MISMATCH (`sql/question_ddl.sql` missing) | Created `sql/schema.sql` covering questions, games, users; traceability references it. |
| THIN_REQUIREMENTS (features w/o FRs) | Added implied feature ids FR-2…FR-6 (intro movie, main menu, fraction questions, ending scene, admin update) and traced each to files/tests. |
| UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT (ASR-2) | Added ASR-2 row (security: local-only, no network, hashed-ish session identity) in TRACEABILITY.csv. |
| GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS | Documented concrete per-technology rationale in adaptation table (not copy-pasted). |
| DUPLICATE_BLOCKS | Normalised single canonical copies (openapi/proto/sql) in DESIGN_DECISIONS only. |
| PLATFORM_CONFLICT | Whole document adapted to desktop (this table). |
| UML_SYNTAX (participant/artifact, `->>`) | Treated participants as objects, artifact→component/container, `->>` → `->`; mapped classes unchanged. |

## 3. Assumptions (spec is thin)

- **Space Fractions** is an educational fraction game for a single local user (End User) with an optional Admin role for updating questions.
- A **round** = a series of N fraction questions (default 10, configurable) drawn at RANDOM and shuffled; score = correct/total. State machine Playing/Paused/GameOver follows the spec's states/transitions.
- Questions are both **seeded** (data/questions.json, ≥20 items covering types: compare, addition, subtraction, multiplication, simplify, identify) and **code-generated** at runtime: math fraction questions where the correct value is computed in code and validated independently in tests. Wrong choices are distinct and never equal to the correct value.
- Question kinds: `compare` (which is larger/smaller), `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `simplify`, `equivalent`. Each generated item stores its operands so tests can RECOMPUTE the expected answer.
- **Admin** updates questions via an admin screen (add/edit/delete), persisted to SQLite; generated questions are not editable (computed) but seed/added questions form the pool.
- "Introductory movie", "main menu", "ending scene with feedback" are realised as Tkinter screens (intro/title with animated stars, menu, results/ending screen with score + encouraging/calibrated feedback).
- 1000 concurrent users / 1-hour sessions (A1, A2) are not applicable to single-user desktop; noted as non-goals. Session time is not enforced.
- Persistence: scores history in `games` table; questions in `questions` table; profile in `users` table (ASR-1 durability).

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class / test |
|---|---|
| Actor End User | `user/user.py::User` |
| Actor Admin | `admin/admin.py::Admin` |
| Class Game (id, score, play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py::Game` |
| Class Question (id, prompt, options, getPrompt(), getOptions()) | `question/question.py::Question` |
| Class User (id, username, playGame(), viewScore()) | `user/user.py::User` |
| Class Admin (id, username, updateQuestions()) | `admin/admin.py::Admin` |
| Game --* Question composition | `Game.questions: list[Question]` |
| User --* Game composition | `User.current_game: Game` |
| Admin --* Question composition | `Admin.updateQuestions()` managing pool |
| States Playing/Paused/GameOver | `game/state.py::GameState` enum + `GameStateMachine` |
| Transitions (start→Playing, pause, resume, gameOver) | `game/state.py`, tests `tests/test_state_machine.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play/getPrompt/answer/result) | `game/service.py::GameService` + `ui/screens/game_screen.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin update → success) | `admin/admin.py` + `ui/screens/admin_screen.py` |
| Activity diagram (play→score→display) | `game/round.py::Round` |
| Use cases Play/View Score/View Help/Update Questions | `ui/screens/{menu,game,results,help,admin}_screen.py` |
| Components GameComponent/QuestionComponent/UserComponent/AdminComponent | packages `game/ question/ user/ admin/` |

## 5. UI design brief

- **Target users**: children/students aged ~8–12 (End User) learning fractions, plus a teacher/parent (Admin) who updates questions. Single local user.
- **Mood**: bright, playful, encouraging, space-themed (fits "Space Fractions" title) — a fun learning game, not a serious test.
- **Colour palette** (roles):
  - background: `#0B1026` (deep space navy)
  - surface: `#1B2144` (panel background)
  - primary: `#4A90E2` (buttons, accents)
  - accent: `#FFD166` (stars, highlights, score)
  - secondary accent: `#9B5DE5` (space purple)
  - success: `#43D17C` (correct feedback)
  - error: `#FF5D73` (wrong feedback)
  - text: `#F4F6FF` (light, high contrast)
  - muted text: `#A9B4D6`
- **Fonts**: Tk defaults via `tkinter.font`; sizes: title 40 bold, subtitle 26, main content 26, buttons 20, inputs 20, feedback 24. Use `('Segoe UI', size, weight)`.
- **Layout**: fixed full window (minsize 1100x750, centered, maximized). Each screen a `tk.Frame`; navigation via controller `ui/app.py`. Title header bar top, content center, big buttons bottom. Canvas space background with animated stars drawn on `<Configure>`.
- **Key screens**:
  1. IntroScreen (introductory movie: animated starfield + title + "Start").
  2. MenuScreen (main menu: Play, View Score, Help, Admin, Quit).
  3. GameScreen (prompt + typed OR multiple-choice input, big submit button, Enter submits, input auto-clears, immediate green/red feedback).
  4. PauseScreen / HelpScreen (paused state, resume).
  5. ResultsScreen (ending scene: score, calibrated feedback — no praise for 0, stars for high score).
  6. AdminScreen (list/add/edit/delete questions, validate all fields).
  7. ScoreHistoryScreen (past scores from SQLite).
- **Feedback policy**: correct → green "Correct!" with the right value; wrong → red showing the expected value of the *just-submitted* item (computed before state advances). Ending screen rating matches actual score (0 = "Let's practice more", high = celebratory stars).
